note: Like Thai: balay (house), bah-LAI.
Like how: sabaw (soup), sah-BOW.
oo gliding into a quick y, like gooey said in one beat: luy-a (ginger), looy-ah.
Like boy: baboy (pork; pig), BAH-boy.
ee gliding into a quick w. The line writes eew.
Said ch when a vowel follows: otso (eight), oh-choh.
Said j when a vowel follows: dyip (jeepney), jeep.
Always hard in Cebuano words, as in go. Before ee or eh the line writes gh: ginikanan (parents), ghee-nee-kah-nahn.
A quick tap, like the tt in American butter: diri (here), dee-REE.
u-lan: u early in the word, a as in father. Stress on the last syllable.
pu-la: two full vowels. Stress on the last syllable, not the first as English would put it.
da-ko: o in the last syllable. The q is a final catch: stop the breath, add no k.
pu-ti: p and t with no puff of air. Ends in a catch.
ga-may: g hard, as in go; ay as in Thai.
ka-poy: k with no puff of air; oy as in boy. Stress on the first syllable.
u-haw: the h is said; aw as in how.
bug-naw: u early in the word, g hard; aw as in how.
hu-gaw: u early in the word; aw as in how. Stress on the first syllable.
ti-il: two vowels side by side are two syllables, with a catch between them.
tam-is: the hyphen marks a catch before the i.
tan-aw: a catch after the hyphen, then aw as in how.
ngi-pon: ng starts the word, as in singer; o in the last syllable.
lung-sod: ng as in singer; u early in the word, o in the last syllable.
da-gat: g hard; both a's as in father. Stress on the first syllable.
di-ri: r is a quick tap. Stress on the last syllable.
